title: The Rootless Weaving

features.name: the stopped loom
features.desc-on-touch: Threads hang in the air where hands left them. You find yourself understanding the pattern only by the absence of its completion.

features.name: textile vines
features.desc-on-touch: Woven strips have rooted themselves and begun growing like slow plants, pattern and plant becoming indistinguishable in the dark.

features.name: knot memory
features.desc-on-touch: A single knot tied and retied, each loop holding a different decision. You remember being here before, but the knot has changed.

features.name: wind-caught threads
features.desc-on-touch: Fabric strips catch nothing, move nothing, but they still remember the shape of wind. Watching them is like reading a story that ended before you arrived.

features.name: weaver's hands
features.desc-on-touch: Palm-prints in dust, muscle memory left behind. The hands that made this weaving learned that stopping is also a form of pattern.

features.name: thread-light
features.desc-on-touch: Where strands cross, they hold light like water in cracks. The weaving has become a map of where it broke.

inscription: the roots let go; the weaving learns to hold itself

file.name: HandWeaving_LoamStation_1970s_FieldRecording.wav
file.note: Loom shuttles and weaver's breathing, slowly fragmenting into pure rhythm. The second half is silence interrupted by thread-hum.

reverie.title: REVERIE — the shed where thread learned its own length
narr: Your fingers find the warp, forty threads pulled tight.
She's outside, framing shots of how the light breaks
through the weave, how every gap holds a story.
You ask why she won't weave, just photograph. She says:
"Weaving is already a photograph. It just takes longer."
You pull the shuttle through. The rhythm is a kind of answer.

exits.label: the weaving sleeps upward, cycles returning
down where the threads tangle into root
toward a place where patterns refuse to repeat
back to where hands still remember their work
